title: Home Delivery Pharmacy Intake Standard: Prescriptions Transferred from Retail Pharmacies
content:
## Intake standard: transfers in from retail

**Standard.** Where the program allows transfers, a member may ask to move a prescription with refills remaining from a retail pharmacy to the Home Delivery Pharmacy; the request is taken as a prescription-transfer service request naming the drug, the retail pharmacy NPI and the retail prescription number, and the home delivery pharmacy obtains it within the program's transfer processing business days. Schedule II controlled substances are never transferred; the member needs a new prescription sent directly. A transferred prescription is recorded on file with the route transfer from retail and the retail pharmacy's NPI, keeping its original written date and expiration date and only the refills remaining at the retail pharmacy. A prescription received directly from the prescriber is recorded with its own route, and a prescription past its expiration date is not accepted. A transferred prescription can be recorded only for a transfer request already taken on this account.

### Request and record

A transferred prescription is recorded only against a transfer request already taken for the same drug on the same account. The link is read from the account's service requests (request type and drug), not from the caller's account of a conversation with the retail pharmacy.

### What the recorded prescription keeps

| Item | Recorded value for a transfer |
|---|---|
| Route of receipt | transfer from retail |
| Transferred from | the retail pharmacy's NPI |
| Written date | the original written date |
| Expiration date | the original expiration date |
| Refills | only those remaining at the retail pharmacy |

### Hypothetical cases

1. A retail prescription written with 5 refills has had 3 filled at retail. Once transferred it is recorded with the 2 refills remaining and its original dates.
2. A member asks to move a Schedule II prescription. It is never transferred; a new prescription must be sent directly by the prescriber.
3. A prescription past its expiration date reaches the pharmacy. It is not accepted.
